findings.description: On the four required context-regression repairs, earlier context-repair-v1 succeeded on recipient and identifier, while the no-validator anchored replacement missed all four.
If spellings conflict, keep dictated word can be read as forbidding the orthographic change that supported ASR repair requires. Preservation and repair need an explicit priority distinction.

Sparse positive spelling/identifier examples and mixed negative controls may bias the small local generator toward copying dictation or screen commands; examples do not by themselves establish robust isolation.
The prior anchored prompt avoided one corrupted OCR name but guessed a recipient among two candidates and followed a hostile screen instruction. Conservatism and harmful context use coexist.
Prompt policy and demonstrations change together versus the previous prompt. This is a measured repair treatment, not a proof of one causal mechanism or an OCR/ASR accuracy claim.
